answer.label: Not Nikola Tesla — an unsourced modern attribution
answer.sourceLine: This line turns up in none of Tesla’s documented books, articles, patents, letters, or interviews. It is absent from Wikiquote’s Nikola Tesla page altogether — not even in its Disputed or Misattributed sections — and a Tesla research archive lists it among “quotes pending to verify.” A fact-check found no source and concluded Tesla “probably didn’t say it” ↗, noting it spreads mainly through paranormal and New Age accounts. Treat it as an unsourced modern attribution, not a Tesla quotation.

author.name: Nikola Tesla
author.heading: About Nikola Tesla
author.bio: Nikola Tesla (1856–1943) was a Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer whose alternating-current systems and wireless-power experiments helped build the modern electrical age. His later, sometimes mystical public statements made him a magnet for metaphysical-sounding sayings. This quote fits that pattern — a “study the unseen” sentiment pinned to his name without any documented source.

misattribution.heading: A classic Tesla-magnet quote
misattribution.intro: Nikola Tesla is one of the internet’s most-abused names for feel-good and metaphysical “quotes.” This line is a textbook case: emotionally resonant, science-adjacent, and completely unsourced.

items.why: The exact sentence appears in none of Tesla’s books, articles, patents, letters, or recorded interviews, and it is absent from Wikiquote’s Tesla page entirely ↗.

A fact-check ↗ found no reputable source and noted the line is propagated chiefly by accounts linked to the paranormal, part of a broader habit of attaching spiritual-sounding lines to famous scientists like Einstein and Edison.

misattribution.truthLine: Until someone produces a dated Tesla book, letter, or interview containing it, this is best described as an unverified modern attribution ↗ — not a Tesla quotation.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Tesla
lead: Tesla’s real biography — a visionary who spoke of wireless energy, cosmic forces, and technologies decades ahead of his time — makes almost any grand, mystical prediction sound plausible in his voice. That plausibility is exactly what lets unsourced lines like this one attach themselves to his name and travel unchecked.

The quote also flatters a specific audience: it seems to grant scientific authority to the study of “non-physical” forces — consciousness, spirits, psychic energy. That built-in appeal, more than any evidence, explains its popularity.
context.pull: Emotionally resonant, science-adjacent, and completely unsourced.
